title: Air Quality Location Pin: Coordinates for AQI
description: Pin a place and copy stable coordinates for air-quality lookups with the Air Quality Location Pin — for OpenAQ and AQI services. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a researcher tracking one neighbourhood's air pins it once and reuses the same coordinates in every AQI platform — the station data changes, the pin does not.
quick_answer: The Air Quality Location Pin gives stable latitude and longitude for a place so you can run air-quality lookups on open AQI platforms that think in coordinates. Pin the place, copy the pair, use it in your AQI service — the coordinate step, done once and done exactly.

faq: Are AQI values shown here?
No — this page provides the coordinates; AQI readings live on the open air-quality platforms the coordinates are for. The division is deliberate and stated on the page.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — pin a place by searching or clicking; your browser's own location is only used if you ask a tool to use it.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Place data varies by source. The coordinates are the stable part — names are labels pinned to them.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No. The pin is yours to copy; nothing about your position is kept by this page.
Which AQI services take coordinates?
Open, coordinate-based platforms such as OpenAQ-style services and most air-quality APIs — paste the pair wherever a lat/lng is asked.
How precise should the pin be?
Four to five decimals (about 1–10 m) suits station-level questions; two decimals names the district. Match precision to the question.
Can I pin several places?
One at a time here; lists belong to the Batch Geocoder, which returns coordinate tables.
The nearest station is far away.
Then the platform's reading is a regional estimate — the pin still asks precisely; the answer's coarseness is the network's, and worth knowing.
Can I pin a school or workplace?
Any place with a location can be pinned. Sensitive places deserve the same discretion online as off — pin the area, not the classroom, for public posts.
Do coordinates expire?
No — the pin is stable by design. Stations open and close around it; that is the platform's changelog, not yours.
